description.de: Vom Ende der letzten Kaltzeit bis zu frühen bäuerlichen Gemeinschaften. Die Kapitel vergleichen Wohnen, Sammeln, Anbau und Tierhaltung in verschiedenen Regionen. Mesolithikum und Jungsteinzeit bezeichnen regionale Entwicklungen mit unterschiedlichen Zeitgrenzen.
description.en: From the end of the last glacial period to early farming communities. The chapters compare dwelling, foraging, cultivation and herding across regions. The Mesolithic and Neolithic describe regional developments with different time boundaries.

sourceRefs.locator: Gregory IX.42; Epistolae 914, first paragraphs and final appeal: Chlothar’s resources, Agnes’s election, obedience of the founder, protection of property, and burial in the church dedicated to Mary even if unfinished.
Carmina XI.19, Latin text, translation, recipient and historical context: milk and other delicacies, a doctor’s orders and the closing greeting.
ER 1931, Gregory IX.40, text and Discussion: the clerics’ mission probably in 568, Eufronius of Tours, and the reception in Poitiers in 569.
Introduction and “Playing the crowd”, “Beyond the gates”, “Reaching east”: Fortunatus and Baudonivia, the donations (Vita I.12–13), the Rule and communal gifts, and the eastern mission (Vita II.16).
Attestation 933, Gregory, Glory of the Confessors 104: he went to Radegund’s community at Poitiers on hearing of her death.
Notice pddn_hagio.202110061928562430200, Mort and Éléments d’identification: Radegund died at Poitiers in August 587.
IX.39, opening: Clotild, Basina, the group’s departure from Poitiers and appeal to Gregory in Tours, followed by the bishop’s version of his answer.
X.16, pp. 123–126: complaints, Leubovera’s answers, Didimia confirming her gift to the abbess and the judges’ reasons for retaining her.

X.16, from De palla quod repotarent to donatrix Didimia confirmavit: a silk wrap brought de parentibus (from her kin) was given to the abbess. The account distinguishes the original wrap, the altar covering and the trim.
Section on the nuns of Poitiers, pp. 136–142; narrative setting of the 589 appeal, inserted letters in IX.39–42 and the episcopal tribunal of 590 in X.16.
Folio 31v, Poitiers BM 250 (136), Lieu de conservation, Période de création and Descripteurs iconographiques: Poitiers, c. 1100, Radegund withdrawing to the monastery.
Summary and licensing; file history, 2 May 2008: digital image from the municipal library at Poitiers, 1,082 × 850 px, faithful photographic reproduction under the Public Domain Mark.

labels.de: Radegunde und die Frauen von Poitiers
labels.en: Radegund and the women of Poitiers

summary.de: Eufronius von Tours brachte die Reliquie in das Kloster von Poitiers.
summary.en: Eufronius of Tours brought the relic into the Poitiers convent.

summary.de: Gregor kam beim Tod der Gründerin nach Poitiers.
summary.en: Gregory came to Poitiers when the founder died.

labels.de: 589 · Die Nonnen sprechen bei Gregor vor

summary.de: Gregor schildert den Versuch einer Gruppe von Nonnen, ihre Beschwerden aus Poitiers anderswo vorzutragen.
summary.en: Gregory recounts the nuns’ attempt to take their complaints to someone outside Poitiers.

summary.de: Im Bericht aus Poitiers bekommt die Seidenspende eine Zeugin mit Namen.
summary.en: The report from Poitiers names a woman who testified about her gift of silk.

summary.de: Eine Äbtissin schickt Milch, ein Bischof bringt eine Reliquie, eine Nonne sagt über ein Stück Seide aus. Briefe und ein Urteil erlauben Einblicke in das Leben hinter den Klostertoren.
summary.en: An abbess sends milk, a bishop brings a relic and a nun testifies about a piece of silk. Letters and a verdict give a glimpse of life behind the convent gates.

sourceRefs.locator: Fr. 8 in Fragmenta Historicorum Graecorum. Naissus and the five deserters, monoxyles and the storm, Bleda’s wife and thanksgiving gifts, encounter with the former merchant at the residence.
p. 31 and n. 5, on Priscus as secretary to Maximinus in summer 449, the sequence of known towns and unnamed villages and the unknown location of Attila’s wooden palace.
Sections Lady Sak K’uk’ and K’inich Janaab Pakal I, fig. 112, the Oval Palace Tablet, and the entry specifying Long Count 9.9.2.4.8 (615), birth in 603, accession aged twelve and the debated regency.
Object description: oval tablet, House E, Sak K’uk’ offering a royal headdress to her son; nineteenth-century cast from the original.
World Heritage property 411. Location line for Palenque in Chiapas and coordinates 17°28′59.988″ N, 92°2′60″ W; an orientation for the site.
Ch. 4 in the translation of Cave and Coulson, p. 130. Separate prices for ordinary grain and the king’s stocks, numbers and weight of loaves, and the final provision on unfree dependants.
Date and editions, Boretius, no. 28, pp. 73–78; ch. 4, grain and baked bread at Frankfurt in 794.
Chapter 5.2, printed pp. 183–186, especially the keelson’s incomplete 104th ring on p. 184, the repair sequence and the summary on pp. 185–186; fig. 55 compares excavated Dublin ship parts.
First three paragraphs, covering crew, oak, tentative origin in the Dublin area around 1042, and 60 oars.

Journal of Korean Art and Archaeology 5, pp. 105–108, site coordinates on p. 105, table 1 for quantities, fig. 3 for cargo tags and fig. 4 for the Qingyuan weight. pp. 107–108 discuss Hakata, Tōfuku-ji, Hakozaki and the possible rebuilding fund.
Dendrochronologia 31, pp. 266–272. Abstract, species identification and matching of 21 boxes to western Japanese cedar chronologies.
Exhibition introduction. The vessel sank off Sinan in 1323. The site came to light in 1975 and was excavated from 1976 to 1984.

Opening paragraphs on the Nika fire, dedication on 27 December 537, architects, vault, 558 collapse, 562 rebuilding and decoration. Closing paragraphs on conversion under Mehmed II in 1453 and subsequent Ottoman additions.
Building history, from the conversion of the patriarchal cathedral under Mehmed II in 1453 to the successive Ottoman minarets.
Opening discussion of Rhomaioi and the capital; “The Latin Occupation of Constantinople” and “Late Byzantium” on 1204, 1261, Nicaea and Trebizond.

Opening paragraph on the commemorative plaque at Pino Suárez and República de El Salvador, the comparison of possible locations and the concluding identification of the southern approach to Tenochtitlan, 8 November 1519.

Book XII, chapter 16. Opening place-names, garlands and necklaces, Moteuczoma’s welcome, Marina interpreting the answer, and the list of the lords accompanying Moteuczoma. This English excerpt presents the later Nahua account.
Second letter to Charles, excerpt pp. 85–89. Bridge and removable beams; attendants prevent physical contact; later speech in the lodging as reported to Charles.
Archaeological Research in Asia 23, article 100195. Comparison of Fuzhou, Hangzhou and Ningbo by composition and form of the ceramic assemblages, and conclusion.
Geographical data, component 1443bis-021, Ningbo Sanjiangkou river confluence.
Bibliographic note Segunda Carta. The letter is dated 30 October 1520 in Segura de la Frontera; first printed at Seville in 1522.
Subsection Loma Caldera Eruption, cites McKee’s radiocarbon estimate at Cerén at 95% probability, AD 610–671. This dates a single eruption, not a decades-long volcanic episode.

Site setting and methodology, figs. 1–5 and discussion of Household 1. Wattle-and-daub buildings and thatch, dental plaster casts, manioc between Structures 6 and 11, field cultivation south of the village, fixed hearth and vessel contents in Structure 11.
Brief Synthesis and map coordinates, dossier 675, 13°49′39″ N, 89°22′9″ W. Seventh-century farming settlement preserved beneath the Loma Caldera eruption.
Printed p. 627, entry beginning Her kyð on þissere bec. Old English text and translation: Ongynethel and Gythiccael, half a pound, four pence, two officials, church door and altar, named witnesses.

Scope and Content, post-Gospel additions: 51 records of manumission in Latin and Old English, marginal and blank-leaf entries. The catalogue’s broad dating should be read with Pracy’s discussion of individual hands and names.
The Haskins Society Journal 31, pp. 1 and 9, especially notes 40–43. Competing datings for entries sharing the name Maccos, around 1000 or late in the eleventh century.
National Heritage List for England 1355166, Location and Details, grid SX 07313 67033. The standing church is later than the entry and is used to locate Bodmin only.
CUL T-S 20.47. Translation, opening dating clause and list of scrolls and textiles. Details identifies the language of the inventory as Judeo-Arabic.
Description and translation of T-S 20.47, 1r. The inventory dated 8 Tammuz 1391 Seleucid records objects owned by the Iraqi congregation and stored in the Palestinian synagogue in Fustat.
Synagogue, item 3, inventory dated 1080, T-S 20.47. Schoolroom, item 2, letter T-S Ar.53.65, separately dated to the eleventh or twelfth century.
Translated letter and catalogue data for T-S Ar.53.65, including the note about the child’s writing board.
Account of the foundation of the Fatimid city in 969 in relation to the older settlements.

Chapter III.1.b, Tätigkeitsbereich des Brückenmeisters, pp. 22–23 and notes 62–65. Petition of the citizens and Herbord, exemptions from toll, twelve-foot exclusion zone, divided fines, bishop and duke.
Timeline on pp. 16–17, especially completion by 1146 and the 1182 privileges governing access, duties and maintenance.
Accession 38.40.243. Object description, dimensions, turquoise opaque glaze, date, the excavated site of Sabz Pushan, and the 1938 division of finds.
Map of Nishapur and Environs and the section on excavation of the Sabz Pushan residential quarter.
Unit 6, The City of Nishapur, introductory account and discussion of games and household objects recovered in excavations.

Paragraph beginning “A certain woman from Metz” (Paquette, her family and the Parisian goldsmith); “The Khan’s palace at Karakorum” (the silver tree, bellows, trumpet and servers); “Description of Karakorum” (grain and livestock at the gates). Translation published in 1900.

Introduction, Historical background and city access discussion at fig. 7. Location on the Orkhon, residence under Ögödei, Rubruck’s visit in 1254, east-gate roads and dense settlement outside the walls. Published online 2021.

summary.de: Priskos kam durch Naissus. In der Nähe übergab ein römischer Befehlshaber der Gesandtschaft fünf Männer. Der Punkt markiert die Stadt. Attilas spätere Residenz ist räumlich ungewiss.
summary.en: Priscus passed through Naissus. Nearby a Roman commander handed five men to his embassy. The map locates the town. The residence reached later in the journey cannot be securely placed.

summary.de: 615 trat der zwölfjährige Pakal in Palenque die Herrschaft an. Eine Tafel im Palast zeigt seine Mutter Sak K’uk’ bei der Übergabe des Kopfschmucks.
summary.en: Twelve-year-old Pakal acceded at Palenque in 615. In the palace, a tablet portrays his mother Sak K’uk’ offering him the royal headdress.

labels.de: 794 · Wie viel Brot für einen Denar?
labels.en: 794 · How much bread for one denarius?

summary.de: In Frankfurt erließ die Versammlung Regeln für Getreide und Brot. Die Zahlen geben die Vorschrift wieder. Einen tatsächlichen Einkauf überliefern sie uns nicht.
summary.en: The assembly at Frankfurt set rates for grain and bread. These figures come from the ordinance. An individual purchase would require further evidence.

summary.de: Der Baum für die Maststütze wurde im Mai oder Juni 1042 gefällt. Das Schiff wurde damals oder bald darauf in Ostirland gebaut, wahrscheinlich im Raum Dublin. Die Karte zeigt die Region der vermuteten Werft.
summary.en: The oak for the keelson was felled in May or June 1042. The ship was built then or soon afterwards in eastern Ireland, probably around Dublin. The map locates the likely region of the yard.

labels.en: 1323 · A trading ship between three coasts

summary.de: Qingyuan ist der wahrscheinliche Ausgangshafen. Das Wrack liegt bei Sinan. Die Tempelgemeinschaft in Kyoto ist als Empfänger auf einem Etikett bezeugt.
summary.en: Qingyuan was the likely port of departure. The wreck lies off Sinan. A cargo tag names a temple community at Kyoto as a recipient.

labels.de: 1453 · Die bisherige Kathedrale wird zur Moschee
labels.en: 1453 · The former cathedral becomes a mosque

summary.de: 1453 ließ Mehmed II. die Hagia Sophia als Moschee einrichten. Der Bau der alten Kathedrale blieb an seinem Platz.
summary.en: In 1453 Mehmed II had Hagia Sophia converted into a mosque. The fabric of the old cathedral remained in place.

labels.de: 1519 · Moteuczoma II. und Cortés am südlichen Zugang
labels.en: 1519 · Moteuczoma II and Cortés on the southern approach

summary.de: Zwei Berichte über die Begegnung führen an den südlichen Zugang zur Inselstadt. Der Punkt bezeichnet die Gegend des Damms.
summary.en: Two accounts of the encounter lead to the southern approach to the island city. The point marks the general area of the causeway.

summary.de: Was verraten ein Schiffsbalken, ein Brotpreis und ein Frachtetikett über die Menschen, die sie hinterließen? Sieben Stationen führen vom spätantiken Balkan bis nach Tenochtitlan.
summary.en: What can a ship timber, a bread price and a cargo tag tell us about the people who left them? Seven stops lead from the late antique Balkans to Tenochtitlan.

description.de: Die Kapitel zur Völkerwanderung führen durch die spätrömische Welt. Die Funde an der unteren Weichsel reichen in die römische Kaiserzeit zurück und gehören zur Vorgeschichte der Reihe.
description.en: These chapters follow the Migration Period in the late Roman world. Evidence on the lower Vistula goes back to the Roman Imperial period and introduces the earlier history of the series.

sourceRefs.locator: Histories II.9, Merovech, Childeric and the tradition about Chlodio; II.37–38, the fighting near Poitiers and honours at Tours; III.1 and IV.22, the divisions and royal seats.
Inv. 56.460, Description and Matières et techniques: inscription, costume, loss on 5 November 1831, wax impression in Ms. 609 fol. 63v, its rediscovery in 1857 and production of the gilt electrotype.
Namur copy R6A.0608, printed p. 96 (signet) and p. 322 (insect ornaments); catalogue account of the 1655 publication.
pp. 43–47 and 56–61. Distance from Poitiers in Gregory’s narrative, Vouillé and Voulon among the proposed battle locations.
No. 1, pp. 1–2: opening list of protected people and church property; injunction on ring-sealed episcopal letters for captives taken under the king’s peace and the truth of petitions.
BK 6, Date, Captions and Transmission: November 587 and preservation in Gregory IX.20. Nineteenth-century editions give the 29th; the map uses the year.
Attestation 933, Gregory, Glory of the Confessors 104: he went to Radegund’s community at Poitiers on hearing of her death.
Notice pddn_hagio.202110061928562430200, Mort and Éléments d’identification: Radegund died at Poitiers in August 587.

Gregory IX.42; Epistolae 914, first paragraphs and final appeal: Chlothar’s resources, Agnes’s election, obedience of the founder, protection of property, and burial in the church dedicated to Mary even if unfinished.
BK 9, Date and Transmission. Editions by Pertz and Boretius date the edict to 18 October 614. Manuscript Berlin, Staatsbibliothek, Phill. 1743.
No. 9, p. 22, c. 12, and p. 23, final subscription and dating clause. Judges from other provinces or regions, restitution from their own goods, and Paris as the place of issue.
ARTEM 4505, Archives nationales K 1 no. 7/1, regest and ll. 3–7. Abbot Dodo, the donor Dagobert, whose father was Baddo, and a plot described as within the walls of Paris.
Object description, first paragraph. Found near Thorn in 2009, struck at Maastricht around 625, its two inscriptions and moneyer.
pp. 227–231, figs. 5, 6 and 9, n. 12. Waterlogged graves at the eastern farm, winter 703/704 felling date for freshly worked oak of grave 27, and the excavator’s dating of the burial to early 704.
Objektfotografie and Copyright → Hauptbild for inventory 1989-0011-0769-9000. The holding museum licenses its main image under CC BY-SA 4.0. No individual photographer is credited on the record.
ARTEM 4511, Archives nationales AE II 6 (K 2 no. 3). Header, regest and ll. 3–4, naming the king’s parents Dagobert and Nanthild as buried in the basilica. Clichy, 22 June 654.
No. 2921, Paris AN K 4 no. 7: original parchment; opening line names Pippin and Attigny, the following pleading names Fulrad, Ragana and her representative, the conclusion dates by Childeric.

Heading, opening and dating clause: 1 March 752, Verberie, rex Francorum. Narrative: Loba’s testament, Gislemar’s admission and surrender per festucam, Fulrad, and the preceding hearing before King Chilperic.
“The Carolingians”, opening paragraphs and notes 35–37, 46: late testimony about 751, Boniface, and papal letters recalling the anointing of Pippin and his sons in 754.

labels.en: The Merovingians and the Frankish kingdoms

summary.de: Das Grab wird gewöhnlich um 481/482 angesetzt. Der Stich von 1655 überliefert das Bild des verlorenen Originals.
summary.en: The burial is usually dated to around 481/482. A print published in 1655 preserves the design of the lost original.

summary.de: Die beiden Heere sind in derselben Gegend bezeugt. Beide Lesepfade öffnen die Schlacht bei Poitiers im selben Jahr.
summary.en: Both armies are attested in the same area. Both reading paths open the battle near Poitiers in the same year.

summary.de: Im Sommer tagten Bischöfe in Orléans. Nach Chlodwigs Tod traten seine Söhne die Nachfolge an.
summary.en: Bishops met at Orléans that summer. After Clovis died, his sons succeeded him.

summary.de: Paris, Orléans, Reims und Soissons dienen Gregor als Bezugspunkte für die Anteile von vier Brüdern.
summary.en: Gregory names Paris, Orléans, Reims and Soissons as seats of the four brothers.

summary.de: Im August wurde Radegunde bestattet. Im November kam der Vertrag von Andelot zustande. Cahors stand im Vertrag.
summary.en: Radegund was buried in August. The treaty followed at Andelot in November. Cahors was named in its clauses.

summary.de: Chlothar II. ließ nach der Vereinigung der Teilreiche in Paris ein Edikt ergehen.
summary.en: Following the reunion of the kingdoms, Chlothar II issued an edict at Paris.

labels.en: 625 · A plot of land and a coin

summary.de: Die Schenkung betrifft Paris. Die Münze mit dem Namen Madelinus wird um 625 nach Maastricht datiert.
summary.en: The donated property lay in Paris. A Maastricht coin bearing the name Madelinus is dated to around 625.

summary.de: Die Urkunde stammt aus Clichy. Der König nennt Saint-Denis als Ruhestätte seiner Eltern.
summary.en: The charter was issued at Clichy. The king identifies Saint-Denis as the place where his parents were buried.

summary.de: Das Eichenholz der Grabkammer wurde im Winter 703/704 gefällt. Das umgearbeitete Bett gehört zu ihrer Ausstattung.
summary.en: The chamber oak was felled in the winter of 703/704. The converted bed was placed inside the chamber.

labels.de: 751 · Wer ist im Juni der König?

summary.de: Die Attigny-Urkunde datiert nach Childerich III. Den Ort der Königserhebung Pippins überliefert eine spätere Erzählung.
summary.en: The Attigny charter dates by Childeric III. A later account supplies the location for Pippin’s elevation.

summary.de: Ein zweites Urteil für Abt Fulrad nennt Pippin im März 752 König der Franken.
summary.en: Another judgment for Abbot Fulrad calls Pippin king of the Franks in March 752.

summary.de: Papst Stephan II. salbte Pippin und seine Söhne. Der Bildvergleich im Kapitel stammt aus dem 13. Jahrhundert.
summary.en: Pope Stephen II anointed Pippin and his sons. The picture discussed in the chapter dates from the thirteenth century.

summary.de: Von Childerichs Siegelring bis zu Pippins Salbung. Zwölf Kartenstationen verbinden Königsfamilien, Münzmeister, Nonnen und Dorfbewohner. In Vouillé und in Poitiers lässt sich mitten im Geschehen das Kapitel wechseln.
summary.en: From Childeric’s signet to Pippin’s anointing. Twelve map stations connect royal families, moneyers, nuns and villagers. At Vouillé and Poitiers you can change chapters in the middle of the story.

sourceRefs.locator: Sections ‘Völker, Stämme, Volksstämme’ and ‘Wanderungen’ on the conventional 375–568 frame, changing groups and negotiations with the empire.
pp. 192–195. Jordanes, Getica 4.25–29, sixth-century setting, possible oral elements and the limits of the Scandinavian origin narrative.
pp. 228–230. Accounts of the lower Vistula in Roman-period sources and in Jordanes.
Olbia R-23 assemblage and fig. 19. Regional ceramic traditions and imported wares in the excavated contexts.
31.4.1–13. The two embassies, imperial recruitment hopes, boats, river conditions and food shortages.
Entry ‘Alaric’, opening extract. The formation of Alaric’s following and the sack of Rome in 410.
Hydatius under 409 and 411 for Hispania. Prosper under 439 and 442 for Carthage and the settlement.
Act XIII, pp. 259–261, lines 1–6 and 29–38. Regnal date, crops, names of the sellers and their marks.
p. 532, introduction and notes 4–8, on Wulfila at Constantinople in 360.
Pars posterior 65–71, reception at Rome, the senate, public expenses and the water supply of Ravenna.
Sections The four gospels in the Gothic language and Materials. Fourth-century translation, probable Ravenna production in the early sixth century, purple parchment, silver and gold inks.
Docs. 35–36, pp. 278–279. Copy preserved in a tenth-century manuscript, subscriptions of King Reccared and Queen Baddo at Toledo in 589.

labels.de: Die Völkerwanderung auf der Karte lesen
labels.en: Reading the Migration Period on the Map

summary.de: Antike Autoren und ein Gräberfeld geben unterschiedliche Hinweise auf Menschen im heutigen Nordpolen.
summary.en: Ancient writers and a cemetery offer different kinds of evidence for people in what is now northern Poland.

summary.de: In der weiteren Region finden Archäologen ähnliche Keramik. Zwischen einzelnen Werkstätten und einem politischen Verband liegen mehrere Deutungsschritte.
summary.en: Archaeologists find related ceramics across this region. Evidence for individual workshops and for a political community calls for different kinds of interpretation.

summary.de: Das Konzil von 360 verbindet den Bischof mit der kaiserlichen Hauptstadt.
summary.en: The council of 360 places the bishop in the imperial capital.

summary.de: Auf der anderen Seite der unteren Donau lag römisches Gebiet. Ammianus schildert die Aufnahme einer Gruppe und die Zurückweisung einer zweiten.
summary.en: Roman territory lay across the lower Danube. Ammianus describes one group gaining admission and another being turned away.

summary.de: In Rom lässt sich ein einzelner Schauplatz benennen. Für vandalische Gruppen auf der Iberischen Halbinsel bleibt die Ortsangabe viel gröber.
summary.en: At Rome the evidence names a specific city. The location recorded for Vandal groups in the Iberian Peninsula is much broader.

summary.de: In der römischen Hafenstadt wechselte die Herrschaft. Erst für spätere Jahre wird hier ein größerer politischer Raum gezeigt.
summary.en: Rule changed in the Roman port. The map shows a larger political territory for later years.

summary.de: Etwa fünfzig Jahre nach der Einnahme Karthagos verkauft ein Paar Nutzungsrechte. Die Holztafel trägt eine Datierung nach dem Regierungsjahr eines vandalischen Königs.
summary.en: Around fifty years after the capture of Carthage, a couple sells cultivation rights. The wooden record dates the transaction by a Vandal king’s regnal year.

summary.de: Der Senat und Papst Symmachus empfingen den König in Rom. Seine Residenz blieb in Ravenna.
summary.en: The Senate and Pope Symmachus received the king in Rome. His residence remained at Ravenna.

summary.de: Gregor nennt den zehnten Meilenstein von Poitiers. Die Lage des Schlachtfelds ist umstritten.
summary.en: Gregory mentions the tenth milestone from Poitiers. The precise battlefield is disputed.

summary.de: Während in Recópolis Glas verarbeitet wurde, traten die Bischöfe flussabwärts in Toledo zusammen.
summary.en: While glass was being worked at Reccopolis, the bishops gathered downstream at Toledo.

summary.de: Wo lassen sich Goten und ihre Nachbarn zu einem bestimmten Zeitpunkt tatsächlich fassen? Zehn Kartenstationen führen von den Gräbern an der Weichsel über den Schwarzmeerraum und die Donau bis zu den Höfen von Ravenna und Toledo. Für 410 sind Rom und Hispania zugleich zu sehen.
summary.en: Where can we place Goths and their neighbours at a particular moment? Ten map stops lead from cemeteries on the Vistula through the Black Sea region and across the Danube to the courts of Ravenna and Toledo. In 410 Rome and Hispania can be seen side by side.

description.de: Die Kapitel zur Völkerwanderung führen durch die spätrömische Welt. Die Funde an der unteren Weichsel reichen in die römische Kaiserzeit zurück und gehören zur Vorgeschichte der Reihe.
description.en: These chapters follow the Migration Period in the late Roman world. Evidence on the lower Vistula goes back to the Roman Imperial period and introduces the earlier history of the series.

sourceRefs.locator: In The Fortified Viking Age, pp. 78–80, fig. 5 and tables 1–2. Riverbank lane before 720, plots 6–8 m wide, Rhineland barrels reused in wells, sequence of individual coin finds and the predominance of Series X from about 725.

European Journal of Archaeology 18, pp. 497–523. The reassessment of the 1985–86 excavations at Sct Nicolajgade 8 uses domestic activity and building remains to propose early permanent occupation on part of the market site.

Early workshop c. 700–720, later workshop c. 760–790. White from bubbles in remelted gold-leaf backing glass and evidence for adding colourants on site.

Chapters X–XI. Witmar as a witness, loss of the books en route, permission to preach, captive Christians, Herigar and his church. The narrative is used for the visit. Modern site identification follows the Swedish History Museum.
Opening paragraphs. Rimbert wrote about 865–875. The museum dates Ansgar and Witmar’s first journey to 830 and distinguishes it from Ansgar’s later visit.

“What do the motifs on the Oseberg tapestry signify?”, “Exotic goods from Persia and Byzantium” and “The colours that disappeared”; clothing strips, the reversed silk, tools and Sofie Krafft’s 41 drawings of 110 silk pieces.
Project introduction and research areas 1–3. Over 80 figured fragments, visible motifs, faded dyes and questions about how the original scenes fitted together.
Opening account of the burial and the four sleighs, followed by “Carvings and ornamentation”. The museum distinguishes three richly carved sleighs and discusses their use before burial.
Hull and rowing holes, the ship built in 820, burial of two women in 834 and the uncertainty over their identities and status.

U841.4 and U842.2, two camps and continued presence; U870.6, four months at Ail Cluaithe; U871.2, Áth Cliath, the leaders, 200 ships and the three groups brought back as captives; U902.2 and U917.4, the defenders driven out and Sitriuc’s entry. U980.1 and U983.2, the battle of Tara and later coalitions.

EMAP Report 7.1, printed pp. 53–55, discussion of captive-taking, trade in enslaved people at Dublin, possibilities of domestic enslavement or onward sale, and the limits of the evidence for different destinations.
Section 2.1.1–2.1.2, printed pp. 3–4. The two placenames, proposed camp by the pool, events of 902 and 917 and changing focus around the Liffey shore at Fishamble Street and Wood Quay.
EMC 1065.0059, obverse and reverse. Entries for ruler, York mint, Raven / Small Cross type, moneyer Æthelferth, spelling on this specimen and weight of 1.17 g.

Rollason, historical sources, the capture in 866–867 and Northumbrian councillors; Blackburn, coinage under Olaf, fig. 82.2 and discussion of the Raven issue under the two Olafs. Craft synthesis, 16–22 Coppergate, pp. 476–481.

“The Jelling Stone”, translated inscription and photographs. The museum dates the raising to c. 965. Harald’s parents and claims about Denmark, Norway and Christianity, earlier Christian objects and Harald Klak’s baptism at Mainz in 826.

Antiquity 97, 1262–1278. Table 1, introduction on the north mound, “Ravnunge-Tue and the Jelling stones”, figures 9–10, “Sources of error” and conclusion. Læborg’s signed dedication and proposed attribution of Jelling 2, weathering at Jelling 1, variants of Thyra’s epithet, and limits of the proposed reburial. The authors give 959/60 for wood from the chamber.

Danish Journal of Archaeology 3(2), pp. 168–170, tables 1–2 and discussion immediately after table 2. Mid-tenth century up to c. 960 for Jelling 1. The chamber wood is reported as 958/59. Historical dating proposals for Jelling 2 differ.

Figures 2–6 and English summary under “Stone for his parents” and “Small silver cup”. Vertical and horizontal writing, reliefs, purple silk, and the 4.3 cm silver cup with gilding and entwined animals from the north mound.

Nature 601, pp. 388–391. Three worked pieces of wood, the metal-tool cuts and Norse depositional context, Table 1 and Fig. 2 on the radiocarbon signal and counting rings to the surviving outside edge. Published online in 2021.

“Discovery of the Site and Initial Excavations (1960–1968)”. Turf construction in eight buildings, bronze ring-headed pin in a cooking pit, stone lamp and spindle whorl in another building, ship nails and iron slag.
Collection entry “Bog Iron Nail, L’Anse aux Meadows, Newfoundland”. Slag and iron from the excavated nail support smelting of local bog ore. The four nails illustrated on that page are reproductions.
Appendix 1, pp. 30–31, manuscript witnesses AM 544 4to and GKS 1005 fol., and “B. Differences”: one planned expedition in Eiríks saga rauða and four in Grœnlendinga saga.

Introductory chronology, “Geographical areas of the Norse settlements and settlement pattern” and “Natural resources”. The written sources place one migration from Iceland to Southwest Greenland under Erik the Red around 985. The Western Settlement was in the Nuuk region; archaeological and radiocarbon evidence in the Eastern Settlement reaches at least the mid-fifteenth century.

Printed pp. 183–186, keelson sample D2-4 and its final spring ring; pp. 187–189, “Parallels in Irish and English ship-finds”, esp. fig. 55 (Fishamble Street stems T357/T364 and corresponding elements of Skuldelev 2) and text on parallels in Danish-built vessels.
Opening account, dating the build to around 1042 in the vicinity of Dublin through the oak tree rings.

Collection overview, paragraphs on wooden pathways and property boundaries, reused ship timbers in dock walls, drains and paths; the Fishamble Street amber worker’s floor with several hundred flakes and splinters.

Printed pp. 146, 148–149 and 152–153. P. 146 describes the transmitted attestations of 1409, 1414 and 1424. Document 49 gives the three Sunday banns, local and foreign witnesses, and the two clerics’ seals. Document 52 names the four men who attended in 1408 and attested in Iceland in 1414. Facsimile of the edition with facing original text and Danish translation.

“Kirkens vinduer” on the round arched east window and other flat lintels; “Brylluppet i Hvalseyfjordens kirke” on the September 1408 wedding, the document at Garðar in 1409 and the journey back to Iceland.
Collection item DMR-217737, ruin 1, group Ø83, NKAH 4427 (Hvalsey church). Location field 60.82883° N, 45.78261° W. Modern survey photograph dated 1935.

Section “Segmented metal foil beads”, pp. 161 and 165 and fig. 5a–c (e.g. ASR9x113 59). Manufacture, silver foil, amber-brown and colourless outer glass, joined segments and the visible structure of broken specimens. Opening section on the continued small-scale production in the ninth century.
Object 106842_HST, accession 34000, Bj 515. Find context, excavator, 1877, silver and glass. The 2021 exhibition label gives the proposed reading of the Arabic inscription.

Scanning 37, pp. 131–137. Materials, p. 132 and supplementary fig. S1, for burial layout, oval brooches, clothes, position and approximate date. Results and figs. 1–3 for filing marks and composition. Discussion accompanying fig. 4 for the favoured dedication and the conditional reading “God willing” if a missing stroke is supplied.
Media ID ba934209-835b-4b3c-ab7a-73126a4375a9, direct association with object 106842_HST, named photographer and CC BY 4.0 licence.
The Archaeology of York 17/5, table 11 and pp. 341–345, figs 140–142. Context, needle binding, shaping the heel, worn sole and outline of a probable patch.
SC1981-7_SF13517, catalogue 1309; coverage c. 930–975, madder at the ankle and no dye elsewhere.
The Archaeology of York 17/11, pp. 1787–1788, 1800–1803 and figs 843–844. A 4B pit, dyes and needles, including their concentration on Tenement C and a previously unused silk offcut.

The Archaeology of York 8/5. Abstract and Period 4B on the properties; Structure 5/1, pp. 622–624 and fig. 212; provisional building chronology p. 798. The report dates wall timbers to winter 961/62 and identifies reused wood at the entrance.
Monument MYO5075, Location: British National Grid SE 6044 5169. Converted to WGS84 and rounded for orientation.

“Gorm the Old authored Denmark’s name certificate” and “Two monuments from Danish history”. Gorm’s commissioning formula, the museum’s rendering of Thyra’s epithet, c. 950, and the photograph “The small Jelling stone” by Roberto Fortuna, CC BY-SA 2.0.

Abstract of chapter 12 in Jelling – Monuments and Landscape, pp. 313–332. The smaller stone is no longer in its original position. Excavation during protection works in 2011 re-examined the central area and the position of the larger stone.

SC1365, “Summary” and “Location”; twin summits, 1974–75 excavation, fifth trench on the eastern side, bedding trench, vitrified stone and three radiocarbon determinations in the sixth to ninth centuries. Site coordinates WGS84, 55.936756 N, 4.563298 W.
“Under siege”, identification of the 870 siege of the Rock, the Dublin leaders Olaf and Ivar, and forced removals following the four-month siege.

Chapter 7, pp. 102–108, Figs. 7.2–4 and Table 7.1. Hearth 4A76P west of the brook, 15 grey-green chert flakes one metre west of the fire, the nail one metre southeast. With 1950 as BP reference, the reported two-sigma charcoal ranges are AD 900–910 and 960–1040 for Beta-252632 and AD 990–1150 for Beta-252633. The map uses their outer envelope; occupation was episodic. pp. 115–116 and Tables 7.5–6 describe birds on the other, upper terrace.

Arctic Anthropology 49(1), pp. 68–87, DOI 10.1353/arc.2012.0015. Abstract and Table 1 discuss the site in relation to Beothuk ancestors, the charcoal determinations for hearth 4A76P2 and seasonal harvesting of birds.
First two paragraphs. Archaeological evidence of Indigenous use over six millennia and Dorset camps on the south shore more than two centuries before the Norse.

labels.de: frühes 8. Jahrhundert, vor 720 · Parzellen an einer Gasse
labels.en: early eighth century, before 720 · Plots beside a narrow lane

summary.de: Noch vor 720 lagen am Fluss schmale Parzellen beiderseits einer Gasse. Der Punkt liegt im ausgegrabenen Marktgebiet.
summary.en: By 720 narrow plots stood on either side of a lane by the river. The point marks the excavated market area.

labels.de: um 830 · Ansgar und Witmar erreichen den Hafen
labels.en: around 830 · Ansgar and Witmar reach the harbour

summary.de: Rimbert schildert die Ankunft der beiden Mönche, die Gefangenen und den Ortsvorsteher Hergeir. Der Punkt bezeichnet die Handelsstadt auf Björkö.
summary.en: Rimbert recounts the monks’ arrival and describes captives and the town’s reeve, Hergeir. The point marks the trading settlement on Björkö.

labels.de: 834 · Die Kammer und die Gewebe der beiden Frauen
labels.en: 834 · The chamber and the women’s textiles

summary.de: Das Holz der Kammer datiert die Bestattung in das Jahr 834. Gewebebänder, Seidenstreifen und Werkzeuge erschließen die Arbeit an Textilien, die bereits vor der Bestattung gebraucht wurden.
summary.en: The chamber timbers date the burial to 834. Woven bands, strips of silk and tools provide evidence of textile work and of the use of fabrics before burial.

summary.de: Die Annalen melden, dass Amlaíb und Ímar mit Gefangenen nach Áth Cliath kamen. Sie zählen Schiffe und nennen Gruppen von Verschleppten. Was aus den einzelnen Menschen wurde, steht dort nicht.
summary.en: The annals say that Amlaíb and Ímar brought captives to Áth Cliath. They count ships and name groups of people who were taken. Individual fates go unrecorded.

labels.de: 939–941, Regierungszeit · Der Rabenpenny des Münzers Æthelferth

summary.de: Unter Amlaíb mac Gofraid begann in York die Prägung der Rabenpennys. Einzelne Stücke könnten noch unter seinem Nachfolger entstanden sein. Die Karte zeigt die Münzstadt.
summary.en: York began issuing Raven pennies under Amlaíb mac Gofraid. Some specimens may belong to his successor. The map identifies the mint town.

labels.de: um 965 · Haralds Stein und die Hand des Runenmeisters
labels.en: around 965 · Harald’s stone and the carver’s hand

summary.de: Harald gedenkt seiner Eltern und beansprucht die Christianisierung der Dänen für sich. Die Rillen der Schrift legen nahe, dass Ravnunge-Tue die Runen schlug.
summary.en: Harald commemorates his parents and claims credit for the conversion of the Danes. The carved grooves suggest that Ravnunge-Tue cut the inscription.

summary.de: Die drei Hölzer datieren Arbeiten auf 1021. Nägel, Schlacke und Spinnwirtel bezeugen weitere Tätigkeiten im Lager, deren genaues Jahr offenbleibt.
summary.en: Three timbers date work at the camp to 1021. Nails, slag and a spindle whorl attest other activities there whose precise year is unknown.

labels.de: 1042 · Die Eiche für die Maststütze von Skuldelev 2
labels.en: 1042 · The oak for the keelson of Skuldelev 2

summary.de: Die Eiche für die Maststütze fiel im Mai oder Juni 1042. Der Bau des Langschiffs wird im Raum Dublin vermutet. Zwei in der Stadt ausgegrabene Stevenstücke zeigen vergleichbare Arbeit an anderen Schiffen.
summary.en: The oak for the keelson was felled in May or June 1042. The longship was probably built in the Dublin region. Two stem timbers excavated in the town show comparable work on other vessels.

labels.de: 1408 · Die Hochzeit von Sigríður und Þorsteinn

summary.de: Im September 1408 heirateten Sigríður Björnsdóttir und Þorsteinn Ólafsson in der Kirche von Hvalsey. Die Bestätigung der Geistlichen in Garðar und spätere Zeugenaussagen in Island betreffen dieselbe Ehe.
summary.en: In September 1408 Sigríður Björnsdóttir and Þorsteinn Ólafsson married in Hvalsey church. The Garðar clerics’ declaration and later testimony in Iceland concern the same marriage.

summary.de: Neun Stationen führen vom Markt am Fluss in Ribe über Gefangene in Dublin, eine Königsmünze und einen Runenstein bis zur nordischen Siedlung auf Neufundland. Ein Ausblick führt ins mittelalterliche Grönland.
summary.en: Nine stops lead from the riverside market in Ribe to captives in Dublin, a royal penny, a rune stone and Norse woodworking in Newfoundland. A final stop visits medieval Greenland.

sourceRefs.locator: In The Fortified Viking Age, pp. 78–80, fig. 5 and tables 1–2. Riverbank lane before 720, plots 6–8 m wide, Rhineland barrels reused in wells, sequence of individual coin finds and the predominance of Series X from about 725.

European Journal of Archaeology 18, pp. 497–523. The reassessment of the 1985–86 excavations at Sct Nicolajgade 8 uses domestic activity and building remains to propose early permanent occupation on part of the market site.

Archaeological and Anthropological Sciences 14, article 180. Site and materials, table 1 and figs. 1b, 7–8. ASR 9 Post Office site (55°19′44.7″N, 8°46′08.7″E). Early workshop c. 700–720, later workshop c. 760–790. White from bubbles in remelted gold-leaf backing glass and evidence for adding colourants on site.

Section “Segmented metal foil beads”, pp. 161 and 165 and fig. 5a–c (e.g. ASR9x113 59). Manufacture, silver foil, amber-brown and colourless outer glass, joined segments and the visible structure of broken specimens. Opening section on the continued small-scale production in the ninth century.
Nature 601, pp. 392–396, abstract and DOI 10.1038/s41586-021-04240-5. Single-year radiocarbon calibration placed the expansion of long-distance trade at Ribe around AD 790 ± 10.

Annual Report 2022, “Solar Event Sheds Light on Trade” immediately before “Farming the Desert”. The excavation team describes the AD 775 signal in a floor layer, 140 radiocarbon dates, and numerous imported beads at AD 790 ± 10. The photograph identifies segmented beads.
Kuitems et al., Nature 601, pp. 388–391, fig. 2. Three cut timbers from L’Anse aux Meadows retain bark edges. The AD 993 radiocarbon event and annual rings establish felling in AD 1021.

Antiquity 97, pp. 1233–1248. Introduction, Classification and chronology, Results, Discussion and figs. 2–3. Type 5 sample of 49, 42 certain and 2 probable reindeer identifications. About 0.5% of identifiable workshop waste was reindeer. Trade in finished items and movement of personal possessions are both possibilities. Fig. 3 credits the photographs of four groups to Mariana Muñoz-Rodriguez.
“Koordinate WGS84” gives 54.49104°N, 9.56623°E for the settlement. General orientation for the finds from different places plotted in Muñoz-Rodriguez et al., fig. 2.

Die Ausgrabungen in Haithabu 14. Discussion of the southern boundary, Struktur N7.6, with fig. 190: item 1778, a pointed split plank dated to 885 where a linear feature meets the bank revetment. The report traces the feature towards the harbour structures.
CHNT 2018, abstract and references. The results join excavated positions, ring-pattern comparisons and felling dates and identify major construction in 881 and 885.

Visitor plan, “The Jetty” and “Platform”. Successive landing stages reached deeper water. Smaller links between jetties created trading space. The guide explains which features of the reconstruction represent choices.
European Harbour Data Repository 7, ID_place 27 “Haithabu Hafen”. The published coordinates for the harbour are 54.492°N, 9.569°E. DOI 10.22032/dbt.38393.
Printed p. 107, lines 6–15, Old English. Ohthere gives five days for the passage from Sciringes heal to the port at Hæðum and identifies lands and islands to port and starboard.

Mitteilungen der DGAMN 27, pp. 25–29, esp. p. 28, figs. 1–2. Schild house erected in 1071 above nearly one metre of deposits. At Plessenstraße 83/3, separate excavation of plots with wattle fences and successive renewals at the waterfront.
Figure 2 locates Schild (no. 5) in Schleswig old town, alongside the site at Plessenstraße 83/3 (no. 1) and the medieval waterfront. A rounded point on the old town peninsula provides orientation.

labels.en: On the market street at Ribe and the waterfront at Hedeby

summary.de: Noch vor 720 lagen am Fluss schmale Parzellen beiderseits einer Gasse. Der Punkt liegt im ausgegrabenen Marktgebiet.

labels.de: etwa 760–790 · Ein Tiegel verrät die Farbe
labels.en: about 760–790 · Colour left in a crucible

summary.de: Die jüngere Perlenwerkstatt von Ribe verarbeitete gelbes, grünes und dunkles Glas. An Tiegelscherben aus der benachbarten Grabung lässt sich das Mischen von Farben vor Ort nachweisen.
summary.en: Ribe’s later bead workshop worked yellow, green and dark glass. Crucible fragments recovered in the neighbouring excavation preserve evidence for mixing colours on site.

labels.de: um 790, ± 10 Jahre · Importierte Perlen in Ribe
labels.en: around 790, ± 10 years · Imported beads at Ribe

summary.de: Segmentierte Glasperlen aus dem Nahen Osten tauchen in größerer Zahl auf. Ein Radiokarbonsignal aus dem Jahr 775 verankert die zeitliche Einordnung der Schichten.
summary.en: Segmented beads from the Middle East appear in quantity. An atmospheric radiocarbon signal from 775 anchors the dating of the stratified finds.

labels.en: ninth century · Combs of reindeer antler

summary.de: Die in Haithabu gefundenen Kämme eines frühwikingerzeitlichen Typs bestehen in der untersuchten Auswahl meist aus Rentiergeweih. Die Karte zeigt die Siedlung, in der die Stücke gefunden wurden.
summary.en: Most of the sampled combs of an early Viking Age type from Hedeby are made of reindeer antler. The map marks the settlement where they were found.

labels.de: 885 · Eine Bohle am Hafen von Haithabu

summary.de: Eine angespitzte Bohle an der südlichen Parzellengrenze ist auf 885 datiert. Der Orientierungspunkt markiert die Hafenanlagen.
summary.en: A pointed plank at the southern boundary of a plot dates to 885. The point marks the harbour installations.

labels.de: 1071 · Ein Haus in der Schleswiger Altstadt
labels.en: 1071 · A house in Schleswig old town

summary.de: 1071 wurde im heutigen Schleswiger Grabungsgebiet Schild ein Holzhaus errichtet. Unter dem Haus liegen ältere Ablagerungen menschlicher Tätigkeit. Der Kartenpunkt markiert das Grabungsviertel.
summary.en: A timber house was built in 1071 in the area of the modern Schild excavation. Older occupation deposits lay underneath. The map marks the excavation neighbourhood.

summary.de: Eine weiße Perle aus Ribe verrät das Rezept ihrer Werkstatt. Kämme aus Haithabu und eine Bohle von 885 zeigen, wie Menschen Handel trieben und ihren Hafen umbauten. Die letzte Station liegt am anderen Ufer in Schleswig.
summary.en: A white bead reveals a Ribe workshop’s choice of glass. Antler combs and a plank dated to 885 show how people traded at Hedeby and rebuilt its waterfront. The last stop lies across the Schlei at Schleswig.

summary.en: Compare the spikelet-base traits with the proportion of rice among counted plant remains.

summary.de: Die Schalenreste helfen bei der Bestimmung der Pflanze. Zwei Datierungsbefunde zeigen, warum der Fundzusammenhang zählt.
summary.en: Husk remains help identify the plant. Two age estimates show why the context matters.

labels.de: Torihama · was Töpfe beim Kochen aufnehmen
labels.en: Torihama · what pots absorb during cooking

summary.de: Verkohlte Beläge und Fettspuren zeigen, welche Lebensmittel in einigen Gefäßen erhitzt wurden.
summary.en: Charred deposits and fat residues reveal foods that were heated in some vessels.

summary.de: Pflanzenreste am Jangtse, Vorratsgruben in Nordchina und Rückstände in japanischen Töpfen. Drei Fundorte zeigen, wie unterschiedlich Menschen in den Jahrtausenden nach der Kaltzeit Lebensmittel gewannen und verarbeiteten.
summary.en: Plant remains on the Yangtze, storage pits in northern China, and residues in Japanese pots. Three sites show different ways of obtaining and preparing food in the millennia after the ice age.

labels.en: New Ways of Living After the Ice Age

description.de: Vom Ende der letzten Kaltzeit bis zu frühen bäuerlichen Gemeinschaften. Die Kapitel vergleichen Wohnen, Sammeln, Anbau und Tierhaltung in verschiedenen Regionen. Mesolithikum und Jungsteinzeit bezeichnen regionale Entwicklungen mit unterschiedlichen Zeitgrenzen.
description.en: From the end of the last glacial period to early farming communities. The chapters compare dwelling, foraging, cultivation and herding across regions. The Mesolithic and Neolithic describe regional developments with different time boundaries.

sourceRefs.locator: City-centre excavations, figs. 3–7. Wooden anvil bases with bronze dust, scrap bronze, the silver coin of 1237/38 from Karakorum’s mint, gravel, paving and trade activities.

Introduction, Historical background and city access discussion at fig. 7. Location on the Orkhon, residence under Ögödei, Rubruck’s visit in 1254, east-gate roads and dense settlement outside the walls. Published online 2021.
Coordinate table in the site documentation, row 3 (“The ruins of Karakorum city”). Point within the ancient urban site, distinct from modern Kharkhorin and Erdene Zuu.

Paragraph beginning “A certain woman from Metz” (Paquette, her family and the Parisian goldsmith); “The Khan’s palace at Karakorum” (the silver tree, bellows, trumpet and servers); “Description of Karakorum” (grain and livestock at the gates). Translation published in 1900.
Section on artisans, especially the final paragraph on recruitment for construction under Ögödei at Karakorum and under Khubilai at Shangdu and Daidu.

Brief synthesis and Integrity, property 1389. Liu Bingzhong’s design in 1256; the Palace City, Imperial City, Outer City, seasonal camps, hunting areas, the Tiefan’gan canal and the later summer capital.
“Official letter from Mongol Empire to Japan”, National Archives of Japan 184-0216. Letters transmitted to Goryeo in 1266 and the context of the first expedition.
Chapter on Goryeo, discussion following the suppression of the Sambyeolcho. Mobilisation of engineers and workers and requisition of timber and ships for the expeditions to Japan.
정의 and 내용. The historic Happo district around modern Masan in Changwon; its role in the expeditions of the late Goryeo period.
Summary and 내용 on Happo’s Goryeo-era tax warehouse and the earlier Na-po port in the Masan coastal area.
Section 1, chronology table for Bun’ei 11. Departure from Happo in the tenth lunar month and arrival in northern Kyushu later that month.
SSC-masa, Linked codes, PSMSL station 2044 (35.1975, 128.5764). Modern harbour reference for Masan Bay, rounded to bay scale.

Islamic Art, MSS 727, folio 34a. Artwork Details, Other Notes and “The Jami‘ al-Tawarikh”. Tabriz, 714 AH (1314–15), Arabic manuscript divided between two collections, Ghazan’s commission and Öljeytü’s expansion.

Article, especially the endowment deed of 1309 and its appendices; annual Arabic and Persian copies of six works, quality of paper, collation, binding and boxes. Location in the eastern suburb of Tabriz.
Iranian Studies 50, pp. 819–842, abstract. Early Arabic illustrated manuscript fragments in Edinburgh (Or. ms. 20) and the Khalili Collections (MSS 727), dated 714 AH/1314–15.

labels.de: Ein Silberschmied in Karakorum, ein Buchmaler in Täbris
labels.en: A silversmith in Karakorum, a book painter in Tabriz
1237/38 · A coin from a workshop floor

summary.de: Die Prägung der Silbermünze lässt sich auf 1237/38 datieren. Sie nennt Karakorum als Prägestätte und lag in der Nutzungsschicht einer Schmiede.
summary.en: The silver coin names Karakorum as its mint and dates to 1237/38. Excavators found it in a workshop occupation layer.

labels.en: 1254 · William of Rubruck at the palace

summary.de: Wilhelm beschrieb 1254 die Stadt und einen vom Pariser Goldschmied Guillaume Boucher geschaffenen Silberbaum. Die Karte zeigt das Stadtgebiet.
summary.en: In 1254 William described the city and a silver tree constructed by the Parisian goldsmith Guillaume Boucher. The map locates the ancient city.

summary.de: Liu Bingzhong entwarf eine Residenz für Kubilai. Im späteren Sommerlager des Hofes blieben sowohl feste Mauern als auch Flächen für Zeltlager erkennbar.
summary.en: Liu Bingzhong designed a residence for Khubilai. The site of the later summer capital preserves the wall lines and space allotted to encampments.

summary.de: Von Happo liefen Schiffe mit Menschen aus Goryeo und dem Yuan-Reich nach Japan aus. Der Kartenausschnitt zeigt die heutige Bucht von Masan. Der genaue Anlegeplatz ist ungewiss.
summary.en: Ships from Happo carried Yuan and Goryeo forces to Japan. The map locates the modern harbour at Masan Bay. The precise embarkation point is uncertain.

summary.de: Eine arabische Abschrift aus Täbris ist auf 714 der Hidschra, entsprechend 1314/15, datiert. Der Punkt bezeichnet Raschid ad-Dins Stiftung im Osten der Stadt.
summary.en: An Arabic copy from Tabriz is dated to 714 AH or 1314–15 CE. The point marks Rashid al-Din’s foundation in the east of the city.

summary.de: Bronzestaub in Karakorum, Schiffbauer in Goryeo und die Stiftung eines Wesirs in Täbris zeigen, von wessen Arbeit mongolische Höfe lebten. In Happo beginnt der zweite Blick auf die Ereignisse von 1274.
summary.en: Bronze dust in Karakorum, shipwrights in Goryeo and a vizier’s foundation in Tabriz reveal the work that sustained Mongol courts. The voyage from Happo offers another perspective on 1274.

summary.en: Choose A, B or compare the island routes. Madjedbebe remains independent evidence. The land overlay shows only a selected area in the 65,000 BP scenario.

summary.de: Die Landfläche gehört zum Stand 25.000 BP. Der Küstenpfeil zeigt eine Hypothese für das Umweltfenster 24.500–22.000 BP. Die beiden Datierungen erfüllen unterschiedliche Aufgaben.
summary.en: The land area belongs to the 25,000 BP snapshot. The coastal arrow shows a hypothesis for the environmental window 24,500–22,000 BP. These dates serve different purposes.

summary.de: Ein konkreter Fundbeleg: Spuren in 20 Horizonten, eingeordnet zwischen 23.500 und 21.700 BP. Der Punkt verrät uns keinen gesicherten Anreiseweg.

summary.de: Hydatius nennt die Stadt für 428. Den Hafen, von dem Geiserich 429 in See stach, nennt er nicht.
summary.en: Hydatius names the city in his entry for 428. His account of Geiseric sailing in 429 leaves the port unnamed.

summary.de: Possidius schildert die Belagerung aus der Sicht eines Bischofs in der Stadt.
summary.en: Possidius describes the siege from the perspective of a bishop inside the city.

summary.de: Die Einnahme der Stadt und die diplomatische Einigung über die Gebiete fielen in verschiedene Jahre.
summary.en: The capture of the city and the diplomatic settlement over territory took place in different years.

summary.de: Im Grenzgebiet des heutigen Algerien und Tunesien kamen die Tafeln ans Licht. Der genaue Fundort bleibt offen.
summary.en: The tablets came to light near the modern Algerian–Tunisian border. The exact findspot remains uncertain.

summary.de: Wie gelangten vandalische und alanische Gruppen vom Rhein nach Karthago? Chroniken, ein Brief aus der Zeit der Belagerung von Hippo und ein auf Holz erhaltener Kaufvertrag machen Menschen an den einzelnen Stationen sichtbar.
summary.en: How did Vandal and Alan groups reach Carthage from the Rhine? Chronicles, a letter from the siege of Hippo and a contract on wood bring individual lives into view along the way.

description.de: Die Kapitel zur Völkerwanderung führen durch die spätrömische Welt. Die Funde an der unteren Weichsel reichen in die römische Kaiserzeit zurück und gehören zur Vorgeschichte der Reihe.
description.en: These chapters follow the Migration Period in the late Roman world. Evidence on the lower Vistula goes back to the Roman Imperial period and introduces the earlier history of the series.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening paragraphs on the Chronicle and the Irish annals, Old Norse víking/víkingr and the raiding voyages underlying one sense of the term.
Hull and rowing holes, the ship built in 820, burial of two women in 834 and the uncertainty over their identities and status.
Opening account of the burial and the four sleighs, followed by “Carvings and ornamentation”. The museum distinguishes three richly carved sleighs and discusses their use before burial.
Coordinates field, 59.309° N, 10.453° E, locates the mound rather than the present-day collection.
The large stone, its decoration, the translated inscription, the dating around 965 and the discussion of earlier Christian objects and Harald Klak’s baptism at Mainz in 826.
“Two monuments from Danish history”, sections on Gorm’s memorial to Thyra (c. 950) and Harald’s inscription.
Geographical data table, property 697bis, N55° 45′ 23″ E9° 25′ 12″.

Nature 601, pp. 388–391. Three worked pieces of wood, the metal-tool cuts and Norse depositional context, Table 1 and Fig. 2 on the radiocarbon signal and counting rings to the surviving outside edge. Published online in 2021.
First two paragraphs. Archaeological evidence of Indigenous use over six millennia and Dorset camps on the south shore more than two centuries before the Norse.
Official national historic site point ACPWM, 51.5952777 N, 55.5330555 W; used for the site, not individual wood samples.
Chapter 5.2, printed pp. 183–186, especially the keelson’s incomplete 104th ring on p. 184, the repair sequence and the summary on pp. 185–186; fig. 55 compares excavated Dublin ship parts.
First three paragraphs, covering crew, oak, tentative origin in the Dublin area around 1042, and 60 oars.

Section 2.1.3, “Viking and Norman Dublin”. The two early settlements south of the river, a pool of the Poddle, and a Liffey crossing. Modern city centre used only to orient the probable building region.
Printed p. 229, Skuldelev samples. Geographic position of the Peberrenden blocking, 55°48′ N, 12°4′ E, and the narrow channel giving access to Roskilde.
Description, photograph date (16 February 2004), photographer, original JPG and source licensing section, CC BY-SA 2.0 Germany. The visible timber fragments occupy the foreground metal frame.

labels.de: Was das Holz der Wikingerschiffe erzählt

labels.en: 834 · Two women in the Oseberg ship

summary.de: Zwei Frauen wurden mit dem schon benutzten Schiff und vier Schlitten beigesetzt. Die Karte zeigt den Grabhügel bei Tønsberg.
summary.en: Two women were buried with a ship that had already been in use and four sleighs. The map shows the burial mound near Tønsberg.

labels.de: um 965 · Ein König setzt seine Eltern ins Bild
labels.en: around 965 · A king commemorates his parents

summary.de: Harald Blauzahn ließ Gorm und Thyra nennen und seine Ansprüche in Runen festhalten. Das genaue Jahr der Inschrift ist unbekannt.
summary.en: Harald Bluetooth had Gorm and Thyra named and his claims recorded in runes. The exact year of the inscription is unknown.

summary.de: Nachweisbar wurden drei Bäume im Jahr 1021 gefällt. Bearbeitungsspuren und Fundkontext verbinden die Hölzer mit der nordischen Siedlung an einer bereits lange von indigenen Gemeinschaften genutzten Bucht.
summary.en: Three trees were demonstrably felled in 1021. Tool marks and archaeological context connect the worked wood with the Norse site on a bay long used by Indigenous communities.

summary.de: Der Baum für die Maststütze wurde im Mai oder Juni 1042 gefällt. Das Schiff wurde damals oder bald darauf in Ostirland gebaut, wahrscheinlich im Raum Dublin. Die Karte zeigt die Region der vermuteten Werft.
summary.en: The oak for the keelson was felled in May or June 1042. The ship was built then or soon afterwards in eastern Ireland, probably around Dublin. The map locates the likely region of the yard.

labels.de: wahrscheinlich in den 1070er-Jahren · Ein Schiff sperrt die Fahrrinne
labels.en: probably in the 1070s · A ship blocks the channel

summary.de: Nach mehreren Reparaturen wurde Skuldelev 2 wahrscheinlich in den 1070er-Jahren in der zweiten Ausbauphase der Sperre im Roskilde-Fjord versenkt.
summary.en: After several repairs Skuldelev 2 was probably sunk in the 1070s, in the second building phase of the barrier in Roskilde Fjord.

summary.de: Von den Schlitten im Oseberggrab bis zur Hafensperre bei Skuldelev. Ein Königsstein nennt Namen, drei Bäume in Neufundland liefern ein Kalenderjahr.
summary.en: From the sleighs in the Oseberg grave to the barrier at Skuldelev. A royal stone supplies names and three trees in Newfoundland give a calendar year.

sourceRefs.locator: II.37: tenth milestone outside Poitiers, men from the Auvergne and senatorial families among the dead; treasure taken from Toulouse after the winter at Bordeaux.
pp. 43–47, 56–61: date of the battle, Alaric’s death, Gregory’s tenth milestone and rival identifications at Vouillé and Voulon.
ER 903, About the source: September 506, Caesarius, Alaric’s permission and the representation of absent bishops by priests and deacons.
pp. 295–296 and n. 2: Theudis’s Toledo decree of 24 November 546 and the city’s emergence as a royal residence.
Document 12, Decretum Theudis regis, pp. 262–264: expenses, witnesses, horses, inclusion in the Theodosian collection and Toledo dating clause.
Introduction and Sobre este lugar: foundation in 578 in honour of the king’s son, the commercial street rising to the palace and church, and the site near Zorita de los Canes.

Introduction, paragraphs 1–3: three furnaces south of the palace, earliest workshop dated from the foundation to the first half of the seventh century, vessels, crucibles and workshop and residential samples.
Documents 35–36, pp. 278–279: opening and subscriptions to the 589 profession of faith, including Reccared, Queen Baddo and the confirming edict. The editor identifies the later copy.
Opening account of the assembly on 8 May, participation from Gaul, Baddo’s subscription and discussion of canons 2 (Creed) and 14 (restrictions on Jewish families).
ER 363, About the source: Homoian and Nicene Christians, Reccared’s conversion in 587, the 589 council and manuscript recensions.

summary.de: Alarich II. gab den Bischöfen die Erlaubnis zur Versammlung.
summary.en: Alaric II gave the bishops permission to assemble.

labels.de: 507 · Die Gegend von Vouillé und Voulon
labels.en: 507 · The area of Vouillé and Voulon

summary.de: Gregor nennt den zehnten Meilenstein von Poitiers. Die Lage des Schlachtfelds ist umstritten.
summary.en: Gregory mentions the tenth milestone from Poitiers. The precise battlefield is disputed.

summary.de: Gregor datiert die Wegnahme relativ zum Winter in Bordeaux. 508 ist eine Annäherung.
summary.en: Gregory places the seizure in relation to the winter at Bordeaux. The year 508 is approximate.

labels.en: 546 · The cost of justice at Toledo

summary.de: Theudis datierte seine Verfügung über Gerichtskosten in Toledo.
summary.en: Theudis’s decree on litigation costs carries a Toledo dating clause.

labels.en: 578 · A new town on the Tagus

summary.de: Werkstattreste ergänzen die Nachricht über Leovigilds Gründung.
summary.en: Excavated workshop remains add another perspective on Liuvigild’s foundation.

summary.de: Während in Recópolis Glas verarbeitet wurde, traten die Bischöfe flussabwärts in Toledo zusammen.
summary.en: While glass was being worked at Reccopolis, the bishops gathered downstream at Toledo.

summary.de: Wer fiel bei Vouillé? Was kostete ein Gerichtsverfahren in Toledo? Aus einer Chronik, einem Glasofen und Königin Baddos Erklärung lässt sich der Wandel des westgotischen Reichs ablesen.
summary.en: Who died near Poitiers? How much did a lawsuit cost in Toledo? A chronicle, a glass furnace and Queen Baddo’s declaration illuminate changes in the Visigothic kingdom.

summary.en: Compare the high-dam zone with the city site and open the photo of the Laohuling dam section.

summary.de: Folge dem Wasser von den Gräben bei den Häusern zu den gemeinsam genutzten Abflüssen am Südtor.
summary.en: Follow the water from ditches beside the houses to shared drains near the southern gate.

labels.en: Shimao · a city by a cliff

summary.de: Lies, wie die Lage auf einem Hügel die Stadtmauern und Terrassen prägte.
summary.en: See how its hilltop location shaped the walls and terraces of Shimao.

summary.de: Grasumwickelter Lehm in Liangzhu, Tonrohre in Pingliangtai und steinerne Mauern in Shimao. Drei Fundorte zeigen, wie Menschen das Gelände nutzten und gemeinsam bauten.
summary.en: Grass-wrapped clay at Liangzhu, ceramic pipes at Pingliangtai and stone walls at Shimao. Three sites show how people used their terrain and organized construction.

description.de: Frühe Städte, Fernhandel und Aufzeichnungen zwischen etwa 4600 und 1800 v. Chr. Die Kapitel vergleichen zeitlich und regional unterschiedliche Entwicklungen.
description.en: Early cities, long-distance exchange and record-keeping from about 4600 to 1800 BCE. The chapters compare developments across different times and regions.

summary.de: Neandertaler, Denisova-Menschen und Homo sapiens: drei Geschichten über Eltern, Vorfahren und Verwandte. Vier Fundorte machen sichtbar, was alte DNA verrät. Etwa 120.000–40.000 Jahre BP.
summary.en: Neanderthals, Denisovans and Homo sapiens: three stories about parents, ancestors and relatives. Four findsites show what ancient DNA can reveal. Approximately 120,000–40,000 years BP.

description.de: Gemeinsamer Suchbereich für die frühen Kapitel der Menschheitsgeschichte. Regionale Einteilungen und Datierungen unterscheiden sich; die Kapitel können sich zeitlich überlappen. Ihre Zeitspannen stehen jeweils am Kapitel.
description.en: A shared discovery group for the early chapters of human history. Regional period definitions and dates differ; chapters can overlap in time. Each chapter shows its own time span.

labels.en: York between the mint and the workshop

labels.de: 867 · Die beiden Könige fallen in York
labels.en: 867 · Two Northumbrian kings die at York

summary.de: Osberht und Ælle fielen im März beim Kampf um York. Der Punkt bezeichnet die Stadt. Der Durchbruch lässt sich keinem bestimmten Tor zuweisen.
summary.en: Osberht and Ælle died in the fighting at York in March. The marker identifies the city. The account does not locate the breach at a particular gate.

labels.de: etwa 930/935–975 · Eine Socke in einem Hinterhof
labels.en: c. 930/935–975 · A sock in a backyard

summary.de: Fund 1309 lag in einem Hinterhof der Phase 4B. Stiche umgeben die abgenutzte Sohle. Die Zeitspanne datiert die Fundschicht.
summary.en: Find 1309 came from a backyard in Phase 4B. Sewing outlines a patch beneath the worn sole. The date range applies to the deposit.

labels.de: 939–941, Regierungszeit · Der Rabenpenny des Münzers Æthelferth

summary.de: Unter Amlaíb mac Gofraid begann in York die Prägung der Rabenpennys. Einzelne Stücke könnten noch unter seinem Nachfolger entstanden sein. Die Karte zeigt die Münzstadt.
summary.en: York began issuing Raven pennies under Amlaíb mac Gofraid. Some specimens may belong to his successor. The map identifies the mint town.

summary.de: Die Chronik nennt die Nordhumbrier als Handelnde und Eadred als neuen Herrscher. York dient als Orientierung für das Königtum. Ein Versammlungsort wird in der Quelle nicht genannt.
summary.en: The Chronicle credits the Northumbrians with expelling Erik and records Eadred’s succession. York marks the seat of kingship. The entry gives no meeting place.

labels.de: Winter 961/62 · Die Bohlen eines Hauses auf Grundstück A
labels.en: winter 961/62 · The wall planks of a house on plot A

summary.de: Die jüngsten erhaltenen Ringe ausgewählter Wandbohlen datieren ihre Fällung auf den Winter 961/62. Der Punkt zeigt das Haus, in dem die Hölzer verbaut wurden.
summary.en: Growth rings from wall planks date their felling to the winter of 961/62. The marker shows the house where the timber was used.

summary.de: Zwei Könige fallen vor York. Ein Münzer setzt seinen Namen auf Silber. Unter der Coppergate bleiben die Sohle einer geflickten Socke und die Türschwelle eines Hauses erhalten.
summary.en: Two kings die in the fighting at York. A moneyer names himself on silver. A backyard yields a mended sock, and excavators uncover the threshold of a house on Coppergate.
